name: ConvertBox
tagline: Hosted popups, sticky bars and embedded opt-in forms with visitor targeting rules, dropped onto your site with one script tag.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. ConvertBox has historically sold lifetime access tiers rather than a monthly subscription.

verdictSummary: There is no network here and no proprietary data: a popup is a div, a script tag and a POST to your own endpoint. An agent can absolutely give you a self-hosted embed script that shows an overlay or sticky bar based on URL, scroll depth, exit intent and a cookie, then writes emails to SQLite. What it will not give you in one session is the visual editor, the template library, the multi-step quiz funnels, or the per-campaign A/B testing and reporting that make ConvertBox worth paying for once. If you are fine editing a JSON config instead of dragging boxes, the DIY version covers most of the actual value on one or two sites. If you run client sites and need someone non-technical to change the headline, keep paying.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted script tag that reads a campaign config, shows a targeted popup, bar or inline form, and stores submissions in SQLite with a basic impression and conversion count.
requirements: A server or small VPS to host the embed script and collection endpoint
Ability to add a script tag to your site
An email provider API key if you want captured emails forwarded anywhere useful
Basic comfort editing a JSON config file instead of using a drag-and-drop editor
whatYouLose: The visual editor and template gallery, replaced by you writing JSON and CSS
Multi-step and quiz-style funnels with branching answers, which are much more work than they look
Built-in integrations with a long list of email and CRM tools, so you wire each one yourself
Real A/B testing with significance and a reporting dashboard, not just two counters
Someone else worrying about the script staying fast, cached and not blocking page render
moatNotes: The moat is the editor and the connector list, not the tech. Nobody has ever been locked into a popup vendor by data gravity.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the last twenty percent of a conversion tool is where all the money is: a headline you can change in ten seconds without deploying, forty templates that already look decent, targeting rules you can reason about in a dropdown, and integrations that already speak to your email platform. Agencies and marketers pay so that the person editing the offer is not the person who can edit JavaScript. A one-off lifetime price also makes the comparison brutal, since your DIY version still needs hosting, maintenance and your own attention every time a browser changes cookie behaviour.
notes: Genuinely one of the more clonable categories on this site, because the value is delivered by a script tag you already control. The gap is editor ergonomics, not engineering.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted on-site conversion widget: a small server plus an embeddable script that shows targeted popups, sticky bars and inline opt-in forms on my own websites.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20 with Hono for the HTTP server
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for storage, single file at ./data/boxes.db
- The embed script is plain vanilla JS, no framework, bundled with esbuild to one IIFE file under 15kb minified
- No accounts, no auth beyond a single ADMIN_TOKEN in .env, no telemetry, no third-party CDN

In scope:
1. campaigns.json in the repo root defines campaigns. Each campaign: id, type (modal | sticky-bar | inline), enabled, html headline and body text, button label, CSS overrides, and a rules object.
2. Rules supported: url includes/excludes patterns, minimum scroll percent, delay in seconds, exit intent (mouseleave toward top), show once per N days via a first-party cookie, and device (mobile | desktop | any). Rules AND together.
3. GET /embed.js serves the bundled script with the campaign config inlined as JSON so there is only one request. Cache for 5 minutes.
4. The script renders a shadow DOM host so my site CSS cannot leak in. Modal has an overlay, a close button and Escape to dismiss. Sticky bar pins to the top. Inline mode mounts into an element with data-box-slot.
5. POST /api/submit records campaign id, email, page URL, referrer and timestamp. POST /api/event records impression, close and conversion counts. Both accept cross-origin requests from domains listed in ALLOWED_ORIGINS in .env.
6. GET /admin, gated by ADMIN_TOKEN as a query param, renders a plain server-rendered HTML table: per campaign impressions, conversions, conversion rate, and the last 100 submissions with a CSV download link.
7. Optional forwarding: if a webhook URL is set in .env, POST each new submission to it as JSON. Log and swallow failures, never lose the SQLite row.

Out of scope, do not build: visual drag-and-drop editor, multi-step quiz branching, A/B testing, per-user accounts, email sending, hosted dashboards.

Deliverables: README with a one-line script tag to paste into a site, a seeded campaigns.json with one working example of each type, .env.example, and npm scripts for dev, build:embed and start. Make it run with npm install and npm run dev on a clean machine.
